header: THE HIGH COURT OF SINDH, CIRCUIT COURT, LARKANA
[Mst. Zahida Bano Lashari Vs. Province of Sindh & others]
Petitioner : Through Mr. Noor Ahmed Lashari,
Respondents : Through Mr. Liaquat Ali Shar, Additional
body: ARBAB ALI HAKRO, J.- Through this petition under Article 199 of the Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, 1973, the petitioner, widow of a police constable who died in service, seeks a direction to the respondents to appoint her against the quota reserved for the legal heirs of deceased police employees.

2. The husband of the petitioner, PC/3002 Muzaffar Ali Lashari, joined the Police Department on 20.06.2014 and died of natural causes on 06.12.2020 while posted at Police Lines, Larkana. The petitioner holds the Higher Secondary Certificate. She first applied to the Senior Superintendent of Police, Larkana (respondent No.4), who called for a verification report on 30.06.2021. Thereafter, when the Inspector General of Police, Sindh (respondent No.2), invited applications from the legal heirs of deceased employees under the Sindh Police (Shaheed, Deceased and Permanently Invalidated or Incapacitated Quota) Recruitment Rules, 2021 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Rules, 2021 '), she applied on the prescribed form on 10.02.2022 for the post of Lady Police Constable (BPS-05) before the closing date of 15.02.2022. Her grievance is that the claim has remained undecided ever since.

3. Respondent No.4 has filed comments, and the Deputy Inspector General of Police, Larkana Range (Respondent No.3), has submitted a C.P No.D-207 of 2026 Page 2 of 4 statement to the same effect. They admit the death in service, the relationship, and the timely application. The scrutiny sheet annexed to the comments records that her documents were examined by the Sub- Committee and "found correct", and that hers is the first claim in respect of the deceased. The sole objection is that, reckoned on 15.02.2022, she was 30 years, 01 month and 14 days old, against the prescribed limit of 18 to 28 years, and thus overage by 02 years, 01 month and 14 days. The case was nonetheless forwarded to the Deputy Inspector General on 08.06.2022 and, by him, to the Central Police Office, Karachi, on 29.06.2022. No order on it has been placed before us.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner applied within time, that her claim was found genuine on scrutiny, and that she cannot be left without a decision for years.
5. Learned Additional Advocate General, Sindh relying on the comments, submits that the petitioner was overage on the closing date and therefore ineligible.
6. We have heard learned counsel and reviewed the record.

7. The first question is whether the claim survives the judgment of the Supreme Court in Muhammad Jalal delivered on 26.09.2024, which declared ultra vires the rules and policies providing for the appointment of the widow or child of a deceased civil servant. The Supreme Court has since held that the judgment operates prospectively and does not undo rights that had matured before it.

The Federal Constitutional Court, while refusing leave against orders of this Court, has held that the right accrues on the death of the civil servant and that the application and the letter of appointment are administrative acts.

That pronouncement binds this Court under Article 189 of the Constitution. Here, the death occurred on 06.12.2020, and the application was made on 10.02.2022; both precede 26.09.2024. The respondents, rightly, have not opposed the petition on this score.
General Post Office, Islamabad v. Muhammad Jalal PLD 2024 SC 1276. Province of Sindh v. Azhar Ali 2026 PLC (C.S.) 1221;
Ayaz Ali v. Federation of Pakistan 2026 SCMR
42. Province of Sindh v. Muhammad Rizwan Khan (F.C.P.L.A. Nos.508, 591, 346, 347, 348, 589, 267, 593, 130 and 353 of 2025), order dated 27.02.2026.

C.P No.D-207 of 2026 Page 3 of 4 8. That leaves the objection of age. The application form, issued by respondent No.2 with the advertisement, a copy of which is on the file, contains the following among its general instructions:
"Applicant age shall be calculated from the date of order of Honourable High Court of Sindh in CP D-271/2019 i.e 03.09.2019."

9. The petitioner was born on 01.01.1992. On 03.09.2019, she was 27 years, 08 months and 02 days old, which is within the limit. The comments do not address this instruction at all; age was calculated on 15.02.2022 without a word as to why the date notified to every applicant was not followed. The respondents settled the terms of the recruitment themselves. Having told the legal heirs how their age would be counted, they could not count it differently when the claim came up for scrutiny. A beneficial scheme, once announced, has to be applied evenly to all who fall within it and where two readings are open, the one which preserves the benefit is to be preferred.
The objection, in the form in which it has been taken, cannot therefore be sustained.

10. The petition is also not time-barred. The claim was sent to the Central Police Office in June 2022, and nothing was communicated to the petitioner thereafter. A citizen whose application is kept pending by the department cannot be told that she came late to the Court. In Ayaz Ali, where applications of 2019 and 2022 likewise lay undecided, the Supreme Court directed that they be decided under the policy in force when they were made.

11. At the same time, we are not inclined to make a direct appointment straightaway. The Rules, 2021 lay down a process of testing and assessment before the recruitment committee, followed by approval by the competent authority. Whether the petitioner meets the remaining requirements is for that authority to determine. What this Court can ensure is that her claim is not shut out on a ground that runs contrary to the respondents' own instructions and that it is decided within a fixed time.
12. For these reasons, the petition is disposed of in the following terms: Ayaz Ali (n.2 above).
Azhar Ali (n.2 above).
C.P No.D-207 of 2026 Page 4 of 4 (i) The objection that the petitioner is overage, as worked out on 15.02.2022, is set aside.

(ii) Respondent No.2 shall have the claim of the petitioner for appointment as Lady Police Constable against the deceased quota reconsidered under the Rules, 2021, reckoning her age in accordance with the instruction reproduced in paragraph 8 above; if she is otherwise eligible and qualifies the prescribed test and standards, her case shall be processed for appointment in accordance with the said Rules.
(iii) The exercise shall be completed, and a speaking order passed after hearing the petitioner, within sixty (60) days of receipt of this order.
13. Office to send a copy of this order to respondent No.2 and to the learned Additional Advocate General, Sindh for compliance. JUDGE JUDGE Zulfiqar
